title: Bamako march against French military presence
location: Place de l’Indépendance, Bamako; AFP also reports convoys approaching from other parts of the city.
organizer: Yéré Wolo / Debout sur les Remparts, represented by spokesperson Siriki Kouyaté and activist Adama Ben Diarra in a pre-event announcement; AFP also identifies some organizers as interim legislature members.
participants_original: Anadolu Ajansı: “plusieurs dizaines de personnes”; AFP: “dozens of demonstrators.” No exact number reported in opened sources.
threshold_50_evidence: Attendance is described only as “several dozen/dozens,” which does not establish a minimum of 50. A Reuters estimate surfaced only in a search snippet and is not used as evidence.

start_date.summary: Both sources date the gathering and dispersal to Wednesday, January 20, 2021.

location.summary: Anadolu places those gathered at Place de l’Indépendance in Bamako; AFP also identifies a central square and approaching city convoys.

scope.summary: The described gathering took place in Bamako; evidence does not establish a nationally coordinated event.

organizer.summary: Anadolu attributes the call to civil-society organizations; AFP says some organizers were interim legislature members. Opened Maliweb reports identify Yéréwolo/Debout sur les Remparts, including spokesperson Siriki Kouyaté and Adama Ben Diarra. The Jan12 Le Pays preview describes a press conference announcing the planned march.

demands.summary: Reports describe a demand for French troops/Barkhane to leave Mali and opposition to French policy. They do not establish an explicit demand that Mali’s own government change a policy, so the domestic-state addressee remains unresolved.

participants_original.summary: Both opened reports use only “several dozen/dozens”; neither gives a numeric estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Opened Anadolu and AFP reports describe only “several dozen/dozens,” which does not establish >=50. A Reuters search-only snippet attributes an approximately 1,000-person claim to an organizer, but this worker did not access the article body and does not use the snippet as verified turnout. Root’s separate body retrieval will be recorded separately after this worker freezes.

end_date.summary: Tear gas dispersal occurred on Jan 20, but AFP reports other convoys still approaching; the episode’s physical end is not established.

protester_violence.summary: The reports do not describe violence by protesters; silence is not treated as evidence of no violence.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Both describe police/gendarmes dispersing those gathered with tear gas.

state_response.arrests.summary: Neither opened report states whether arrests occurred; response remains unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: Neither opened report states whether beatings occurred; response remains unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: Tear gas is reported, but no report describes shots; shooting response remains unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: Neither opened report attributes deaths to the response at this gathering; response remains unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Neither opened report describes authorities receiving or negotiating with protest leaders; response remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The state banned and dispersed the gathering, so ignore is not inferred.

notes: Public gathering occurred on Jan 20, but (1) opened contemporary sources describe only “dozens/several dozen,” while a Reuters estimate remains search-only in this worker file, so >=50 is unresolved here; and (2) opened sources state the demand was French troops leaving, not an explicit demand to Mali’s own government. City hall ban and tear-gas dispersal are state responses, not proof of the demand addressee. The Jan 12/19 articles are pre-event announcements, not attendance evidence. No precise duration or ending assigned.
open_questions: Did organizers explicitly call on Mali’s transitional government to end or change its military cooperation with France?
Can an independent contemporaneous source establish that at least 50 people actually assembled, rather than a larger number being prevented from gathering?
Did other convoys reach the square after the reported dispersal, and when did the episode physically end?

end_date.summary: The search-result text provides no duration or physical end; end date remains unknown.

protester_violence.summary: The search-result text does not describe participant violence; unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: The search-result text does not report accommodation at this meeting; the response field remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The search-result text does not report ignore at this meeting; the response field remains unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: The search-result text does not report killings at this meeting; the response field remains unknown.

notes: Retained as a search-only lead because the article title calls it a manifestation and the text says a patriotic meeting was organized at the Bourse du Travail on Jan 28. It may instead describe the formation of a front at a meeting; no evidence yet confirms an open public assembly or 50 attendees. open_questions: Did a public gathering actually take place on Jan 28, rather than only a planning/front-formation meeting?

title: Bamako CDR/M5-RFP caravan demanding release of detained activists
location: Started at CDR headquarters in Djélibougou, Bamako, and proceeded toward Rail-Da in Commune II before police stopped it near CHU Gabriel Touré.
organizer: CDR (expanded by Maliweb/Le Pays as Collectif pour le Développement de la République and by Bamada as Collectif pour la Défense de la République); youth of M5-RFP joined the caravan.
participants_original: HIIK: “hundreds”; MaliExpress: “thousands”; Bamada: caravan departed “in large number” by cars and motorcycles. These are source-attributed qualitative estimates; vehicles are not a count.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened HIIK account reports hundreds demonstrating on Jan 21; contemporaneous local Maliweb/Le Pays says the caravan took place that day, and Bamada’s search excerpt describes it as departing in large number. The separate MaliExpress snippet says thousands. The exact estimate is unresolved, but HIIK’s hundreds exceeds 50.

start_date.summary: HIIK dates the demonstration to Jan 21. Maliweb/Le Pays says the previous day (Jan 20) was the coordination meeting and the caravan occurred Thu Jan 21; Bamada search excerpt likewise says “hier jeudi” in a Jan 22 report.

location.summary: Bamada search excerpt locates CDR HQ in Djélibougou, route via Djélibougou highway toward Rail-Da in Commune II, and police dispersal near CHU Gabriel Touré; exact stopping point/route details are source-attributed.

organizer.summary: HIIK identifies CDR and M5-RFP members; opened Maliweb/Le Pays says M5-RFP youth accompanied the caravan. The CDR acronym is expanded differently in source text: Maliweb/Le Pays says Collectif pour le Développement de la République; Bamada’s search-only excerpt says Collectif pour la Défense de la République. Preserve the variation.

demands.summary: The demand was release of Ras Bath and other detainees; statements criticized transition-authority arrests and asked for pressure on the new authorities.

participants_original.summary: HIIK reports hundreds and a MaliExpress search result says thousands; Bamada describes vehicles and motorcycles on the route, which are not treated as turnout counts. The qualitative estimates differ and no exact count is derived.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: HIIK’s opened retrospective report says hundreds; local search excerpts report thousands/large turnout. The at-least-50 threshold is met on those descriptions, while exact crowd size remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Search-only Bamada text reports police dispersed the caravan with tear gas and attributes a no-arrests statement to a CDR representative. Other response details are not specified; HIIK does not describe the police response.

scope.summary: Reports describe a Bamako caravan; there is no evidence of a national multi-city campaign.

end_date.summary: Search-only Bamada text reports police dispersal near CHU Gabriel Touré, then a later return to CDR headquarters and a request that supporters go home. It does not establish the actual departure of all attendees or the episode’s exact physical end; end date remains unknown.

protester_violence.summary: Bamada describes a peaceful intended procession, but does not fully characterize participant conduct during the dispersal; violence remains unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Search-only Bamada text says police stopped the caravan and dispersed participants with tear gas near CHU Gabriel Touré. HIIK does not give this response detail.

state_response.arrests.summary: Search-only Bamada text attributes to a CDR representative the statement that there were no arrests. This remains a single source claim.

state_response.beatings.summary: Search-only Bamada text reports tear gas but does not describe beatings; unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: Search-only Bamada text reports tear gas but no gunfire; shooting status remains unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: Search-only Bamada text does not attribute deaths to the response at this event; unknown.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Search-only Bamada text reports dispersal and a later return to CDR HQ, but no government reception/negotiation; accommodation remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The search-only report describes police action but does not establish whether authorities otherwise ignored or addressed the demands; status remains unknown.

notes: The Jan 20 CDR/M5-RFP coordination meeting is not the protest. Maliweb/Le Pays and Bamada search excerpts report an actual caravan on Thu Jan 21; HIIK independently says hundreds demonstrated that date. Bamada search text reports tear-gas dispersal and a CDR representative saying there were no arrests, but HIIK does not describe this response. Bamada reports participants returned to headquarters and were asked to go home, which does not establish that all participants left or the physical episode ended; end date remains unknown. A separate Bamada article scheduled a caravan after Friday prayer on Jan 22, but no distinct execution is verified.
open_questions: Was a separate Jan 22 caravan actually carried out, or does the scheduled report refer to an action that was not confirmed?
Can an exact route and crowd estimate be verified from an opened local report?
Were any other response fields documented beyond dispersal and the reported absence of arrests?

title: Gao march against insecurity and for state security/peace-process measures
location: Gao city; search-only reports place route from Rond-point des Martyrs to the governorate.
organizer: Federation of Civil Resistance Organizations of Gao (FORC-G), as described in search-result reporting.
participants_original: Bamada Jan 29 reports “thousands”; another Bamada account says residents turned out en masse; Mali Actu describes women, youth, elders and children among marchers. These reports provide no exact count and share a publisher.
threshold_50_evidence: A contemporaneous Bamada search result reports thousands at the Jan 27 march, with another Bamada account describing mass turnout; this would meet >=50 if the reports are verified, but article bodies remain unopened. Pending source verification.

start_date.summary: ORTM and Mali Actu search results dated Jan 28 describe a march the previous day; Bamada gives Jan 27 directly.

location.summary: All search-result reports identify Gao; Bamada snippet gives the route from the Martyrs roundabout to the governorate.

scope.summary: Reports concern a single march in Gao; no national coordination is established.

organizer.summary: ORTM and Bamada search excerpts attribute the march to FORC-G.

demands.summary: Search results report demands for better security/state services, representation in the peace accord implementation commissions and DDR, and a probe of earlier Gao protest killings. These target Malian state authorities.

participants_original.summary: Mali Actu describes a cross-age group; Bamada search results describe mass turnout and one says thousands. No exact count. Bamada reports are from the same publisher, not independent confirmation.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Bamada’s search excerpt says thousands, but neither body is opened; another Bamada account says mass turnout. Threshold looks supported if verified, but source access is pending.

end_date.summary: Bamada search excerpt describes the route ending at the governorate but gives no time or physical end date beyond the same-day march.

protester_violence.summary: The result describes the march as peaceful; this is search-only reporting.

state_response.accommodation.summary: Search excerpts say the governor received federation leaders after they submitted a declaration; this is reported actual reception, though page text remains unopened.

state_response.arrests.summary: The excerpts do not report event-related arrests; status remains unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: The excerpts do not report beatings; status remains unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: The excerpts describe security forces accompanying/encadrant the march, not dispersal; status remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The excerpts report a governor meeting leaders, so ignore is not coded.

state_response.killings.summary: The 2016 protest killings are a demand motivating this march, not deaths in the Jan 27 event; response remains unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: The Jan 27 search excerpts do not report shots; status remains unknown.

notes: Local-search results report an actual Jan 27 march and direct demands to Malian authorities, with governor reception. Crowd size is qualitative only and source bodies remain unopened, so threshold/source verification is pending. “187 elements” and “25,012 weapons” refer to DDR/security quantities, not turnout. Accommodation is recorded only as source-attributed governor reception; it is not a successful policy concession.
open_questions: Can an opened contemporaneous source verify attendance >=50 and the reported route/demands?
Does the ORTM page provide a numeric attendance estimate?
Was this the same march reported by Bamada, Mali Actu, Benbere and Afrikinfos, and did any later action continue it?
